note: Scripted THETA RUN scenarios. Dates are real; option prices are modeled. 'crisis' runs score the SURVIVOR achievement.

challenges.title: LEHMAN WEEKEND
challenges.brief: Sell premium into the 2008 crash. VIX goes from 20 to 80. Can a short-premium book survive the worst tail since 1987?
challenges.lesson: Undefined risk plus high buying-power use is how accounts end. Size for the tail, not the average.

challenges.title: FLASH CRASH
challenges.brief: A calm tape, then the May 6 flash crash and a summer of elevated vol.
challenges.lesson: IV spikes are when premium is richest -- if you still have buying power to sell it.

challenges.title: VOLMAGEDDON
challenges.brief: VIX at 10, everyone short vol. On Feb 5 VIX doubles in a day and the short-vol ETPs blow up.
challenges.lesson: Low IV rank is the worst time to sell premium big: the premium is thin and the move is not.

challenges.title: COVID CRASH
challenges.brief: The fastest bear market in history: SPY -34% in 23 trading days, VIX to 82, then a V.
challenges.lesson: Defined risk and small size let you stay in the game -- and sell the richest premium of the decade on the way back.

challenges.title: THE GRIND
challenges.brief: A slow, rate-driven bear market with sticky IV around 25-35. No single crash -- just relentless delta.
challenges.lesson: Managing delta (rolling the untested side, skewing deltas) matters more than the entry.

challenges.title: LOW-VOL MELT-UP
challenges.brief: The calmest year on record: VIX below 12 most of the year and the market only goes up.
challenges.lesson: Short calls fight a melt-up; low IVR means small credits. Consider fewer, smaller trades.

challenges.title: EARNINGS SEASON
challenges.brief: A blind earnings season. Find the names with reports inside your expiry and decide: sell the IV crush, or stay away?
challenges.lesson: Earnings IV is predictably crushed, but the move is the risk. Size earnings trades smaller than core trades.
